title: The normalized difference derivation into the diagonal conormal
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let $\delta:X\to X\times_S X$ be its diagonal and $p_1,p_2$ its projections [def-pc-base-change]. Let $I$ be the actual kernel sheaf of $\mathcal O_{X\times_S X}\to\delta_*\mathcal O_X$, and let $C=\delta^* I$ be tensor pullback [def-sc-diagonal-conormal, def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists a derivation $D:\mathcal O_X\to C$ relative to the presheaf inverse image $f^{-1}_{\rm pre}\mathcal O_S$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] with the following normalization. For opens $U\subset X$, $W\subset X\times_S X$ such that $W\subset p_1^{-1}U\cap p_2^{-1}U$ and $U\subset\delta^{-1}W$, any $a\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $s\in I(W)$ with kernel-inclusion image $p_2^*a-p_1^*a$ satisfy $D_U(a)=(\eta_I(s))|_U$, where $\eta_I:I\to\delta_*\delta^*I$ is the canonical tensor-pullback unit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. No universal property or bijectivity is asserted.

proof.text: Take the neighbourhood $W_0$ of the diagonal obtained by the union of affine products in Tag 01KJ. Restrict the actual kernel to $W_0$, where it is the ideal $J$ of the closed diagonal. The quotient $\mathcal O_{W_0}/J^2$ is supported on the diagonal. Its inverse image is a square-zero extension of $\mathcal O_X$ by $J/J^2$, and the two projections give splittings $s_1,s_2$. Their difference is additive and lies in $J/J^2$. Expanding $(s_2-s_1)(ab)$ shows the Leibniz error is a product of two kernel elements, hence zero. They agree on base functions, giving a relative derivation. The maps of sheaves used here commute with restriction.

On each affine closed-immersion chart, tensor pullback of the ideal is $J/J^2$ and its class map is the canonical unit, by the affine conormal sections theorem. These identifications agree on chart refinements because the unit is natural, giving the identification with $C$. For any opens $U,W$ in the statement, restrict further to such charts: the given section $s$ represents precisely $s_2(a)-s_1(a)$. The unit formula therefore gives $D_U(a)=(\eta_I(s))|_U$ locally, hence globally by the sheaf separatedness axiom.
